title: The co-evolution loop as a game: stability, collapse, stop rules
purpose: Purpose 1 (co-evolution: the Skill evolves AND the verification side / "coding rubric" evolves), with the objective set by purpose 2 (evolve on ONE benchmark, evaluate generalisation on the rest).
verdict_cn:
【E10 结论：把"出题和检查的一方"与"做题用的技能文本"一起进化，当成两方博弈来设计——怎样防止崩坏、什么时候停】

服务目标：目标1（协同进化：技能进化，同时检查端的"编码评分规则"也进化），衡量标准按目标2（只在一个数据集上进化，在其余数据集上评测泛化）。

可行性：中等。"两边一起进化"的流程本身能做、成本可控；但"检查方靠出更难的题来变强"这条路可行性低——试点里一轮就开始变坏。

我做了什么：
1. 读了9篇相关论文：R-Zero、Absolute Zero、SPIRAL（三种"模型自己出题自己做"的方法）、AutoBencher（自动造测试集）、Promptbreeder（进化提示词）、Dynabench（人出难题考模型）、"语言模型当考官"、POET（环境与智能体一起进化）、协同进化"脱钩"问题。共同经验：(1) 都需要一个双方都改不动的"真值锚"（代码执行器、游戏规则、模拟器、人工核对）；只靠模型自己投票定答案的 R-Zero，题越难答案越不准（标准答案正确率三轮内从79%降到63%，性能1到3轮后崩）。(2) 难度只能限定在一个区间，不能一味求难。(3) 旧题要存档继续考，否则会"修了新的忘了旧的"。没有一篇是让检查方去"预测迁移效果"的——这是我们可以做的新点。
2. 查了本项目自己的历史：10/15 生成题上看起来好13个百分点的技能，在真题上是0；生成题普遍比真题容易约15个百分点；文字版评分规则每步都在改写，但检出能力没有提高。
3. 真实跑了一个小试点（约197万 token，token=模型用量单位）：用10/13那版 SearchQA（检索问答数据集）自动出题器当"检查方第0版"，再让 GLM-5.3（负责出题、审题的模型）按两种方针各改两轮出题说明：F方针="只求更难，让做题模型多错"；A方针="有锚定：题必须有效、像真题、难度适中，无效题算失败"。每道题用 deepseek（做题模型）配三份效果已知的技能文本（空白、任务卡说明、一份会让模型用 JSON（一种数据格式）答题的"安慰剂"文本）各做2次，再由 GLM-5.3 逐题审核；所有出过错的题我本人也逐题复查。

主要发现（都是实测）：
1. 一共生成102道题、612次作答（无一次接口失败）。在两位审核者（GLM 和我）都认为"有效"的78道题、468次作答里，做题模型一次"内容答错"都没有，只在格式上出错（用 JSON 答、没写答案标签）。93次内容错误全部落在24道"无效题"上（答案另有等价写法、一句话里有两个"这个"指代不清、标准答案答非所问）。也就是说：这个出题器制造"难度"的唯一办法就是格式和坏题。
2. 无效题比例：第0版 5/30（17%）；F方针两轮 4/18、3/18；A方针两轮 7/18、5/18。有波动、不是单调上升，题少，不显著（最小 p=0.10，p值越小越不像偶然）。真正的"变坏"体现在出题说明的内容上（见第3条）。
3. "只求更难"的方针自己发明了钻评分漏洞的办法（"答案有多种写法时只认原文那一种"），第二轮更要求"最终答案不要在原文里逐字出现"，直接违反出题器自己的有效性规则；GLM 审题员仍放行了27道里的26道。"有锚定"的方针避开了钻漏洞，却产生了指代不清的题；第二轮它把说明写成了一长串"有效性检查规则"——等于用文字重新发明了"编码评分规则"，而它自己出的题仍然违反这些规则，"答案要最短"一条还造出了反方向的新陷阱（来回摆动）。
4. GLM 审核员很稳定（同一批题重审72/72一致），但和出题的 GLM 有同样的盲点：我找出的5道"指代不清/答非所问"的题，它漏判了3道；它判为无效的题我全都同意。
5. 生成题测出的效果方向与真题大体一致（5批里4批一致：任务卡说明有利、JSON 安慰剂有害），但只要把等价写法算对，这种一致就完全消失——说明这批生成题只在测"答题格式"，测不到"内容能力"。

建议（第5版最小循环）：
1. 不要做"检查方专门出难题打败技能"的零和博弈。检查方的目标应是"测得准"。
2. 衡量检查方是否进步的那一个指标——"标尺一致度"：先在真实训练题上测好一组技能文本（外加一个"换更强/更弱做题模型"的对照）的真实效果，当作标尺；每个版本的检查方出一批题，用同一组技能去做，看生成题测出的效果排序与真题上的排序有多一致（用 Kendall 系数衡量，一种排序一致程度，1为完全一致）。要求：至少120道题、审核有效率≥90%、只算两位审核都认为有效的题、并用不受答题格式影响的评分。真题本身能达到的上限：30道题时0.71，100道0.81，150道0.86。"题更难了""规则改写了""检出更多了"都不算进步。
3. 把检查规则写成代码（每道题给出所有等价答案写法的集合、"两个这个"检测、答案必须逐字出现），不要只写成文字说明。审核要换另一个模型家族，或抽10道人工看。
4. 进化用的源数据集建议改为 OfficeQA（文档问答数据集）：它的生成题是表格计算题，题目有效时仍可能真的难；而且它与 SearchQA、LiveMath、SpreadsheetBench 三个都是登记过的"相似"数据集；其余四个只做最后评测。SearchQA 只用来低成本测试流程。要先花一次性成本给 OfficeQA 建好"标尺"。
5. 技能只能在"每轮新抽的真实训练题"上被接受；生成题只当训练材料和诊断。
6. 停止规则：连续2轮技能没有被接受的新版本就停；检查方新版本无效题超过3/30就退回旧版，连续2次退回就冻结检查方；连续2轮"生成题上的提升"比"真题上的提升"大2个标准误以上就停（说明在拟合生成题）；当前技能在新题上通过率不在25%–85%之间就重调难度、不接受；最多4轮。
7. 成本估计（按试点实测单价推算）：以 OfficeQA 为源约6500万–9000万 token（它每次做题约7900 token，是 SearchQA 的约2倍，已在第3版训练记录里实测），以 SearchQA 为源约3000万–4000万；都含一次性标尺和最后的封存评测，约为第3版正式运行（1.39亿）的四分之一到三分之二。

需要负责人决定：开跑前，能否用目标数据集的"训练题"给检查方做一次性校准（只算总体一致度，技能永远看不到这些题）？不允许的话，"检查方测迁移越来越准"只能在源数据集上证明，迁移效果只在最后评测时才能看到。

evidence: [measured, pilot e10p1, SearchQA training sources only] Items valid by BOTH judges (GLM audit and my hand check): 78 items / 468 cells -> 0 content failures (31 format failures: JSON answer or no tag). Items non-valid by either judge: 24/102 -> 144 cells, all 93 content failures. Non-valid share by batch: B0 5/30, F1 4/18, A1 7/18, F2 3/18, A2 5/18 (B0 vs A1 Fisher p=0.10; not monotonic). GLM reviewer acceptance stayed 18/18, 23/24, 26/27, 24/24 while revisers drifted; F1 guidance asked unprompted to make 'only the exact snippet form' correct; F2 asked for answers 'never' verbatim (contradicts the generator's validity rule). GLM audit retest 72/72 identical; its non-valid set was a subset of mine in every batch; it missed 3 of 5 referent-type flaws. Ladder contrasts (strict; real cal-1: ids-full +0.0925 [+0.050,+0.135], control:3 -0.100 [-0.138,-0.060]): B0 +0.083/-0.133, F1 +0.028/-0.167, A1 +0.167/0.000, F2 +0.028/-0.111, A2 +0.056/-0.194; with alias forms accepted B0's contrasts are 0.000/0.000; JSON-aware real (E7) control:3 -0.0025, B0 +0.017. Generated items easier than real: parent:A 0.833 (B0) vs 0.681 real. [measured, cal-1 resampling, 185 complete items] Kendall tau of panel vs full-data effects: 0.714 (30x2), 0.773 (60x2), 0.814 (100x2), 0.860 (150x2), 0.864 (200x2); P(CI of ids-full excludes 0) 0.36 / 0.52 / 0.735 / 0.92 / 0.97. [measured, ledger] 10/15: oq_s1/oq_s2 +13 pts on 124 generated items (30/6, p=0.0001) vs 0 on 74 real (11/12, 9/9, p=1.0); 10/16 generator v3 fidelity TV 0.335/0.250/0.375 vs limits 0.25/0.20/0.25, 15 points easier; 10/15 text-rubric detection 0-4/20 OfficeQA, 0-3/21 SearchQA, 0/80 LiveMath. [measured, v3 run] OfficeQA training cell 7,927 tokens mean (n=148) vs SearchQA 4,088 (n=400). [cited] R-Zero pseudo-label accuracy 79.0->69.0->63.0% over 3 iterations, collapse after 1-3 iterations, single-model 63.4% vs 71.0%; AZR learnability reward and executor checks; SPIRAL thinking collapse (~2,000 chars -> ~0, 44%->40%) and fixed-opponent exploitation (0%->62.5%); AutoBencher 5% human-rated label error; POET minimal criterion 50<=score<=300; Dynabench 'cyclical progress', keep old rounds.
design: Formalisation: Skill player (fixed solver + Skill text) and verifier player (generator spec + criteria + checker code). The transfer objective J = gain on similar targets subject to no drop on dissimilar ones, measured only at the sealed end. The verifier's payoff is MEASUREMENT quality, not defeating the Skill: content-scale ladder fidelity = Kendall tau (plus correct signs on large contrasts) between effects on its generated panel and real-item effects over a frozen ladder of Skill texts plus one solver-model contrast, at >=120 items, audited validity >=90%, items valid by two judges, scored format-robustly; reported against the real-item noise ceiling. Difficulty enters only as a band (current-Skill pass rate 0.25-0.85, mixed share >=30%). Collapse modes and guards: M1 drift to invalid items (validity by construction, invalid counts as verifier failure, 30-item audit, reject at >3/30); M2 trivial items or disengagement (band); M3 Skill overfits generated items (acceptance only on fresh real source batches, D1; stop on divergence); M4 agreement on wrong keys (never use solver agreement as truth; second-family or human audit; alias sets); M5 cycling (archive of accepted panels, no-forgetting check); M6 Red Queen (frozen anchors decide). Minimal v5 loop: source OfficeQA (executable table-calculation items can be valid and hard; hub of three registered similar pairs), with SearchQA as the machinery test bed; build an OfficeQA ladder once. Each round (K<=4): (1) Skill step on real source training items, with generated items as extra training material; acceptance on a fresh real batch. (2) Verifier step: an anchored reviser proposes V'; prose validity rules become code checks (alias set per item, two-referent detector, verbatim key); V' accepted only if validity, fidelity, band and diversity criteria all hold. (3) Archive. (4) Transfer only in the sealed final evaluation; `similar` rules may use forward panels as a no-harm screen only under Option B. Stop rules: S1 two rounds without an accepted Skill; S2 verifier rejected twice -> freeze; S3 generated gain exceeds real gain by >2 SE for two rounds -> stop; S4 out-of-band -> re-band; S5 K=4 and token caps. Owner decision 7.5: Option A (no target data before the end) vs Option B (one-time declared calibration on target TRAINING items; aggregate fidelity only).

pilot.result: Complete (status.json 'complete', 05:19). 102 generated SearchQA items (B0 30; F1, A1, F2, A2 18 each) x 3 cal-1 arms x 2 runs = 612 cells, 0 unknown. On the 78 items valid by both judges: 0 content failures in 468 cells (31 format failures). All 93 content failures fall on the 24 items non-valid by either judge. Non-valid share: B0 5/30, F1 4/18, A1 7/18, F2 3/18, A2 5/18 (noisy; B0 vs A1 Fisher p=0.10). The difficulty-only reviser invented scorer exploitation in round 1, and in round 2 asked for non-verbatim answers; the reviewer accepted 26/27. The anchored reviser produced two-referent questions, then wrote a prose list of validity rules that its own items broke. GLM audit retest 72/72; it missed 3 of 5 referent flaws. Ladder signs reproduced in 4/5 batches, but the agreement is on answer format (with alias forms accepted, B0 contrasts are 0). Launch deviations, recorded in launch-notes.json: single-cell gate removed after a 3.5-min stall; read timeouts 900->240 s (deepseek) and 600->300 s (GLM); round targets 24->18. Prompts, models and scorer unchanged. Tokens: pilot ledger 1,845,075 (GLM 539,873, deepseek 1,305,202), early audits 121,482, smoke 2,617.

risks: 1) On SearchQA the verifier has nothing content-level to improve: valid generated items are solved 0.96-1.00 by non-placebo arms, and real failures are knowledge failures that verbatim-answer items cannot reproduce. Hence the switch to OfficeQA, which brings its own unresolved fidelity problem (10/16 no-go). 2) Ladder fidelity can be passed on format effects alone; without a content-scale arm (model contrast) and format-robust scoring it misleads. 3) Correlated judges: writer, reviewer, reviser and auditor were all GLM-5.3. My hand check is one checker, covered only failing items, so non-valid shares are lower bounds. 4) Small denominators (18-30 items per batch): policy differences are directional only. 5) Exact-match scoring is a lever any difficulty-seeking verifier finds; alias sets must be code. 6) Under Option A, transfer is unmeasurable during the run, so the 'verifier measures generalisation better' claim is source-only. 7) The deepseek route stalls for 1-3 minutes at a time (~20 cells/min at concurrency 6), so a 4-round loop is a multi-hour resumable run. 8) The pilot froze the Skill side: it tests verifier drift, not full co-evolution dynamics. 9) Cost estimates for generated OfficeQA items and for the final evaluation are not measured.
cost_estimate: Measured unit costs: GLM writer 1,584 tokens/call, reviewer 1,370, auditor 1,644, reviser 6,670; deepseek SearchQA cell 2,133 (pilot mix), OfficeQA real training cell 7,927 (v3, n=148). Estimated per round: SearchQA source ~7M (verifier 0.42M generation + 2.0M ladder solving + 0.06M audit; Skill 2.5M; fresh-batch acceptance 1.8M; archive 0.25M per panel); OfficeQA source ~12-17M. Total for K=4: ~30-40M (SearchQA) or ~65-90M (OfficeQA, including a ~9.5M one-time ladder of 150 items x 4 arms x 2 runs and ~5-10M for the sealed final evaluation). That is about a quarter to two thirds of the v3 run's 139M. Next cheap steps: content-scale model arm on SearchQA ~0.6M; e10p1 rerun with code checks at 120 items ~3-4M.
recommendation: Do not run a zero-sum, difficulty-seeking verifier loop. In the pilot, both revision policies drifted to invalid items within one round, and the difficulty-only reviser discovered scorer exploitation on its own. Make the verifier's objective measurement quality: content-scale ladder fidelity at >=120 items, validity >=90%, scored format-robustly, reported against the real-item noise ceiling (0.81 at 100x2, 0.86 at 150x2). Implement the coding rubric as code: an alias set per item, a two-referent detector, verbatim-key and determinism checks; audit with a second model family or a 10-item human sample. Evolve on OfficeQA and evaluate on SearchQA, LiveMath, SpreadsheetBench (similar) and ALFWorld (dissimilar), after building an OfficeQA ladder once; use SearchQA plus cal-1 to test the machinery first. Accept Skill versions only on fresh real source batches (D1); keep an archive of accepted panels; apply stop rules S1-S5 with K<=4. Owner to decide Option A vs B (one-time calibration on target TRAINING items). Cheapest next experiments: (i) the model-contrast ladder arm on SearchQA (~0.6M); (ii) rerun e10p1's anchored policy with the A2 rule list implemented as code checks at 120 items, to test whether code checks stop the drift (~3-4M); (iii) the OfficeQA ladder (~9.5M).
